construction.proof:
WHOLE-OWNER RETURN AFTER RELEASING AUXILIARY PATCH WALLS

The predecessor is a complete native packing obtained by gluing complete
published-source patches. Its module boxes prove compatibility, but those
box walls are not actual obstacles to the contained prisms. Retain every
whole owner, its source word and its proper frame. Remove only those
auxiliary box walls. For each pair choose an actual separating direction
from the two sets of prism face normals and cross products of prism edges.
The separating-axis theorem makes this list complete for convex polyhedra.
Every chosen direction must already separate the full predecessor pair.

With these directions fixed, solve one common linear system in all owner
translations and the single host scale: all actual prism vertices must
satisfy every host wall; each pair must satisfy its actual directed support
inequality. Whole source frames and all owner labels remain fixed. The
old packing is a feasible control. Further returns may choose different
already-realized separators from the preceding complete packing; record
every such predecessor and its all-pair directions. No metric angle is a
variable, and no independently optimized marginal state is combined.

Every retained finite witness embeds its complete parent native record and
SHA256, the source mark/word data inherited through that record, all fixed
frames, every realized contact step, and the new complete native packing.
Official exact-input host/all-pair verification is required. Numerical LP
success alone is not certification, and LP failure is not an obstruction.

construction.name: heterogeneous_complete_honeycomb_patch_rows_and_layers
construction.proof:
Whole honeycomb patches with explicit end costs and cyclic layer composition

Use the canonical regular hexagonal prism of base edge one and height L, with planar vertices (+-1,0),(+-1/2,+-sqrt(3)/2). Its standard honeycomb translation lattice has basis (3/2,sqrt(3)/2),(0,sqrt(3)). For positive integers a,b take all ab whole owners with centers
  (3i/2, sqrt(3)*(j+(i mod 2)/2), 0), 0<=i<a, 0<=j<b.
These are lattice words (i,j-floor(i/2)); their interiors are disjoint because the lattice tiles the plane by the whole regular hexagons. Extrusion through the full prism height preserves this separation.

The exact patch box has dimensions
  d0=(3a+1)/2,
  d1=sqrt(3)*(b+epsilon/2), epsilon=1 if a>1, otherwise0,
  d2=L.
The patch's box midpoint is
  (3(a-1)/4, sqrt(3)*(b-1+epsilon/2)/2,0).
In particular both transverse end costs are retained; ab is not treated as a fractional area density. The two endpoint phases of the staggered columns remain present, including a final unmatched column when a is odd.

Treat the complete patch as a module and apply the three proper cyclic coordinate permutations. Type k makes intrinsic axis k vertical, with the other two axes ordered cyclically. At a horizontal event E the module-grid capacity per layer is floor(E/d_i)*floor(E/d_j). A layer word (l0,l1,l2) has actual height H=sum(lk*dk), owner count ab times the sum of those capacities weighted by lk, and common enclosing cube edge S=max(E,H). Place all layers at consecutive closed intervals and center each complete transverse grid. Modules in different grid cells or layers have disjoint box interiors. Within each module the actual honeycomb lattice gives pair separators. A final suffix of complete owners may be deleted, with every parent and retained word recorded.

The finite probe compares complete patch dimensions and integer layer words below the current public/submitted/private target. No metric angle is varied. Proper cyclic quaternions and the canonical owner orientation are fixed before the probe. A prospective gain is promoted only after reconstructing every owner and independently checking the source, all native wall constraints and all pairs. Equal-value and nongain patch states remain controls, not global optimality claims.

Heterogeneous whole-patch rows and layers

This extends HONEYCOMB_LAYER_PROOF.txt by composing different complete honeycomb patches rather than requiring a single patch shape in every layer. Each module has actual ab whole hexagonal-prism owners, with the same source lattice word and full patch boundary costs as before. A fixed proper signed axis permutation puts its bounding box dimensions into (width,row-height,layer-height).

For one exact layer-height h, a row type consists of floor(S/width) identical complete modules at that fixed frame, centered across a common width S. Its cost is its full row-height, and its value is ab times the module count. A row word with summed heights at most S gives an actual layer with that many whole owners: place the closed row intervals consecutively, center the combined rows, and retain their different module widths. Distinct rows have disjoint box interiors.

A layer word with summed full layer-heights at most S then gives a complete cube packing, by placing those layers on consecutive closed intervals and centering the stack. Different layers have disjoint box interiors. Every owner in a module has the inherited honeycomb orientation, further acted on by the module's fixed proper cube symmetry. The grammar's max-plus count is therefore constructive: its full backpointer word is an inverse decoder, not only an upper or density estimate. Deleting a named whole-owner suffix preserves a complete packing.

All costs lie in (p+q*sqrt(3))/2 with nonnegative integers p,q. The finite dynamic program stores (p,q) costs and an actual word, first for rows at one layer height, then for layers. The metric comparison only orders those exact positive costs against the common cube side; no angle or independent physical scale is optimized. A source module that has no count advantage may still occur in an equal-value boundary word and is retained in the candidate bank. The final native witness verifies all actual vertices and pair separation independently of the grammar.
